clue.text: A handicap where the poacher set his snare

definitions.meaning: the ... Handicap is a well-known flat horse race in which runners carry weights to even their chances

definitions.text: where the poacher set his snare
definitions.meaning: the folk song 'The ... Poacher' places its poacher in that English county

explanation.definitionFit: One name serves both a famous handicap horse race and the eastern English county of the folk-song poacher.

clue.text: Hero-worshipper seen on the Thames

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth the youth who swam the Hellespont nightly to his beloved, the priestess Hero
the famous rowing club at Henley-on-Thames bears the same name

explanation.definitionFit: The mythical lover of Hero shares his name with the Henley rowing club whose crews are a regular sight on the river.

clue.text: Draw attention to Angel's middle unadorned

indicators.note: the central letter of the angel is placed in the middle of the word for bare

parts.note: unadorned means bare, naked: nude
G is the middle letter of the five-letter word Angel

explanation.surface: Someone points out an angel figure whose midriff has been left without decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle' works twice over: G is the middle of ANGEL, and it goes into the middle of NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod someone with an elbow is to draw their attention to something.

clue.text: Visually a favourable eyewitness

definitions.meaning: by means of sight, an adverb
read as two words, an optic (eye) that is an ally (a friendly witness)

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means by sight, and split in two it pictures an eye that sides with you.

clue.text: No approval of retreat

parts.note: OK is a word of approval or assent

explanation.surface: A refusal to sanction someone's withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy corner or recess is a retreat where one can hide away.

clue.text: Poirot's friend at the sea-side

definitions.meaning: Captain Arthur ... is the companion and narrator of many Agatha Christie detective stories
a resort town on the Sussex coast of England

explanation.definitionFit: Christie's detective's sidekick shares his name with an English south-coast resort.

clue.text: Groovy Winchester

parts.note: a Winchester is a firearm whose barrel has spiral grooves cut inside it, so it is literally grooved, not trendy

explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester is a famous make of long gun whose barrel is cut with spiral grooves to spin the bullet.

clue.text: Job comes next before his lyrical work

definitions.text: Job comes next before his lyrical work

parts.words: Job comes next before his lyrical work
parts.note: in the Bible the Book of Job comes immediately before the Psalms, the lyrical work attributed to King David

explanation.definitionFit: The composer of the Psalms, traditionally David, wrote the Bible's book of sacred songs that follows Job.

clue.text: Become embarrassed by a Marxist study

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist or Marxist
a den is a private room for study or work

explanation.surface: Someone blushes on reading an essay by a communist author.
explanation.definitionFit: When embarrassed, the face flushes and turns crimson.

clue.text: It is an odd, unusual way to get extras

indicators.note: putting the letters in an unusual way means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A remark that some strange method yields bonus items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual way' rearranges the letters of IT IS AN ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras are things added on, supplements.

clue.text: A vessel to infiltrate the enemy-this way?

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the ship goes inside the enemy

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship sent to slip behind enemy lines, asking whether this is the route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fosse Way is a Roman road across England, so this answer is a 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fosse Way is the famous Roman road running from Exeter to Lincoln.

clue.text: Thoroughly wet, and a beastly draught

definitions.meaning: a dose of liquid medicine given to livestock, a draught for beasts

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to soak through and a dose of medicine poured down an animal's throat.

clue.text: Put cover round New York's beauty, falsely accused

indicators.note: the cover is put round the beauty, enclosing it

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a belle is a beauty, as in the musical 'The Belle of New York'

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly charged, after hiding up a New York beauty queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To libel someone is to defame them with false written accusations.

clue.text: Elaborately compose lyric about Hindhead

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the head letter
to compose is to arrange, so the letters of lyric are rearranged

parts.note: the head of Hind is its first letter, H; Hindhead is also a village in Surrey

explanation.surface: Instructions to write an ornate song about a Surrey village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compose' rearranges LYRIC into RICLY, and 'about' puts it round H, the head of Hind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done lavishly and sumptuously is done in an ornate, rich manner.

clue.text: Anglo-French harmony on the up and up

definitions.text: Anglo-French harmony on the up and up

parts.words: Anglo-French harmony on the up and up
parts.note: the French word for harmony names the supersonic airliner built jointly by Britain and France, which went up and up

explanation.definitionFit: The supersonic airliner jointly developed by Britain and France takes its name from the French for agreement.

clue.text: He wasn't passed over

parts.note: at the first Passover the angel of death passed over Israelite homes but struck the firstborn of Pharaoh's people

explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus, the people of Pharaoh's land were not spared at the Passover, unlike the Israelites.

clue.text: Fish with a pole — plain enough?

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a pole or stick

explanation.surface: An angler goes after fish with a simple rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain as a pikestaff' is an idiom for perfectly obvious, which is why the definition asks 'plain enough?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff' means entirely obvious.

clue.text: Exclusive command of the game

definitions.meaning: sole control of a market or supply

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sole control of a commodity and is the name of the board game of buying streets.

clue.text: Collector of items for a rainy day

definitions.text: Collector of items for a rainy day

parts.words: Collector of items for a rainy day
parts.note: the items are coins saved up, and saving for a rainy day means putting money by for hard times

explanation.definitionFit: A container for coins collects savings put by against hard times.

clue.text: Wine for Tom and Jerry

parts.note: the cartoon pair are a mouse and a cat, and Latin mus (mouse) plus cat names a sweet wine

explanation.definitionFit: The sweet wine's name splits into Latin for mouse and the English cat, the cartoon's pair.

clue.text: Miss Kate did it in winter it appears

definitions.text: Miss Kate did it in winter it appears

indicators.note: the answer appears written out inside the words Miss Kate did

explanation.surface: A young lady went gliding on the ice in winter, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it appears' signals the answer sitting within miSS KATE Did, and the whole clue describes what she did.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding over ice on blades is the classic winter pastime.

clue.text: Colour up and could have died getting the bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

indicators.note: could have suggests the letters of died might have formed something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flushes and feels near death while being booed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RED into DER; 'could have' rearranges DIED into IDED. 'Getting the bird' is British for being jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the bird means being hissed or jeered, that is, mocked.

clue.text: Garage feature where one for the road might be obtained

definitions.text: Garage feature where one for the road might be obtained

parts.words: Garage feature where one for the road might be obtained
parts.note: one for the road is usually a last drink, but here it is a car bought from a dealer's display room

explanation.definitionFit: A car dealer's display area is where a new car for the road is bought.

clue.text: Railway boy climbs the poet's mount

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy from the railway scrambles up a hill associated with a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbs' turns LAD into DAL. Rydal Mount was Wordsworth's home in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Rydal Mount was the house where Wordsworth lived for over thirty years.

clue.text: Maybe there's a name for the book

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters are one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a title could be found for a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges THERES. The answer is also a woman's name, hence 'a name for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Old Testament tells of the Jewish queen of Persia who saved her people.

clue.text: Haven of the Cinque Ports

definitions.meaning: an old English word for a landing place or harbour
one of the medieval Cinque Ports, a group of harbour towns on the Kent and Sussex coast

explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town's name comes from an Old English word for a harbour, and it was one of the Cinque Ports.

clue.text: Mark comes up to school

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means reading from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a note is a mark, as in a note taken or a mark of distinction

explanation.surface: A grade gets reported back to the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns NOTE into the famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English boarding school near Windsor.

clue.text: Was general assistant ?

parts.note: a general's assistant is an aide, so one who served as aide was, as a verb, giving help

explanation.definitionFit: To have helped is to have given assistance, and an aide-de-camp is a general's assistant.

clue.text: Survived due to salt concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of due to salt are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone stayed alive thanks to a salty potion.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lasted longer than others is to have survived them.

clue.text: One of 25's grounds for a famous victory

definitions.text: One of 25's grounds for a famous victory

parts.words: One of 25's grounds for a famous victory
parts.note: Wellington supposedly said Waterloo was won on the sports grounds of the school at 25 down

explanation.definitionFit: Wellington's saying credits Waterloo to the sports grounds of the Thames-side school at 25.
